title: The Fire Station
strapline: Boots on, down the pole, into the engine — nee-naw, nee-naw — a call has come in and the firefighters are ready.
intent: Firefighters are heroes in children's eyes, and role-playing the fire station lets children explore the important people who keep the community safe while feeling brave and capable themselves.
The urgent, physical play — pulling hoses, climbing, carrying, rushing to the engine — is powerful gross-motor exercise with real drama and purpose.
Children learn genuine, useful knowledge about staying safe — what firefighters do, why we stay calm, how to get out and call for help — woven in reassuringly, not frighteningly.
Responding to calls, working the team and taking on roles grows cooperation, communication and the language of urgency and instruction.
The station is full of mathematics — hose lengths, counting the crew, ladder rungs, how far, how fast, how many.
Real vocabulary and community knowledge pour in — firefighter, engine, hose, ladder, rescue, emergency, safe, help.
implementation: Set up a fire station and engine — helmets, boots, hoses (ribbon or real hosepipe outdoors), a bell or siren, a phone for taking calls, ladders to climb.
Take a role in the drama — the caller, the chief, someone who needs rescuing — so children answer calls, plan and respond as a crew.
Model the calm-under-pressure talk: 'There's a fire on Example Lane — how many firefighters do we need? Who's driving the engine?'
Weave in real safety knowledge gently — firefighters help us, we stay calm, we get out and call for help — and welcome a visit from the real fire service if you can.
Bring in maths through the play — count the crew, measure the hose, count ladder rungs, time the rescue with a sand timer.
Extend the story outdoors with water and hoses to 'put out' chalk flames, and add a logbook for recording the calls that come in.
key_questions: There's a fire on Example Lane — how many firefighters do we need?
Who is driving the engine, and who is working the hose?
How long is our hose — can we measure it?
What do we do to stay safe and calm if there's a fire?
How many rungs are on the ladder?

Children count the crew, measure the hose and time the rescue.
Children gain community vocabulary — firefighter, engine, hose, ladder, rescue, emergency.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into the urgent, physical drama of the fire station, taking on the firefighter's role with courage.
They test the props and their own bodies — the hose, the ladder, the dash to the engine.
active_learning: Children stay gripped in the mission, working as a crew to answer the call and complete the rescue.
creating_thinking: Children plan and solve each emergency — who does what, how to reach the fire — and take on real knowledge about keeping safe.
